title: Open issues miss upstream fixes that land after filing
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

An open issue that waits on an upstream change doesn't notice when that change lands. #364 said postgres.js "doesn't expose" a close signal and cited porsager/postgres#1240. That PR closed on 2026-10-29 when the fix shipped in v4.0.0, and triage found it only by checking by hand a day later. Nothing in `scripts/` reads the `owner/repo#n` references in open issues.

## Done when

- A weekly workflow runs a `scripts/` check that lists each open `smonn/db` issue whose body or comments cite another repository's issue or PR (`owner/repo#n` or its github.com URL) that is now closed, and fails when the list is non-empty.
- Its tests use recorded `gh` payload fixtures with `node:child_process` mocked, as `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` requires.

title: Driver pins postgres.js 3, which lacks the dead reserved connection fix
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Problem

We pin `postgres` `^3.4.9`. postgres.js v4.0.0 (2026-10-29) fixes the dead reserved connection behind #364: a released connection stays released, and the pool no longer takes back a terminated one (porsager/postgres#1199 and #1240, closed as "part of v4"). Renovate holds the bump on the Dependency Dashboard (#89).

v4 rewrites the pool, connection, protocol, and socket layers, so it touches the adapter's assumptions: the session reset after `fn`, the raw socket error codes #364's comment lists, transaction handling, and the TypeScript types (now an ES module with named types). It may also change #623's statement caching. Changelog: https://github.com/porsager/postgres/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

## Done when

- `postgres` is `^4.0.0` in `package.json` and the lockfile, and `pnpm check` passes.
- Each v4 change the adapter relies on is checked against its tests, and #364 and #623 say what the upgrade changed for them.

title: chore(deps): update pnpm to v12.16.1
body:
- `pnpm install` now relinks a command that a workspace project renames into the projects that depend on it when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [pnpm/tasks#224](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/224).
- Commands, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm self-update`, and invocations with unknown flags now apply the same `packageManager` and `devEngines.packageManager` settings when switching to the pinned pnpm version or recording it in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. `--config.<key>` flags and `lockfileDir` now reach the version switch and lockfile sync on every entry point. Unreadable settings in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or the global `config.yaml` that do not affect the pin decision no longer block the version switch [pnpm/tasks#222](https://redirect.github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/222).

title: Postgres.js reserve hangs with fetch_types off, so it stays on
body:
## Problem

With `fetch_types: false`, postgres.js 3.4.9 never settles `reserve()` on a fresh connection, so every `session` and `transaction` hangs. In `ReadyForQuery` (`src/connection.js`), the initial-connect branch clears a queued reserve and returns before `onopen`. Upstream tracks it as porsager/postgres#1219, with an open fix in porsager/postgres#1220.

`postgres` is a peer dependency, so users bring their own client and a local patch can't reach them. #365 keeps `fetch_types` on: our built-in array parsers take precedence, and #451 casts enum and domain arrays to text in builder SELECTs. Turning `fetch_types` off only saves the per-connection type fetch and lets raw `sql` read enum arrays as text.

## Done when

- A postgres.js release ships the fix, the peer range requires it, and our `connect()` helper sets `fetch_types: false`, with a cold-pool `reserve()` test.

title: Driver releases a reserved connection whose backend died while idle
body:
## Problem

#359 fixed two cases of #221: the driver now records a dead backend when one of the session's own statements fails with a socket or connection-closed error. One case is still open. If the backend dies while `fn` sends no statement, nothing records the failure. The driver then sends the reset to the dead socket and releases the connection to the pool.

Fixing it needs a close signal for a reserved connection, and postgres.js 3.4.9 doesn't expose one (porsager/postgres#1240). CI run 39947830448 shows the case.

## Done when

- A backend that dies while `fn` is idle is never reset or released to the pool, and a test against real Postgres proves it.
- Or, if postgres.js still has no signal, this issue records the upstream state and the workaround that was ruled out.
